signUpPageInfo.info:
Thanks for clicking to learn more about why we might have this email record on file.

Firstly, please double check that you have entered your email address in correctly.

If we are still showing this email address is already a registered address in our records then the following explanations may be the reason for this:

This new MOORR App has it origins in the original and still active MyWealth Portal desktop platform, which is also the home of MoneySMARTS the hugely popular money management tool, made popular by the best selling book - Make Money Simple Again, the Property Couch Podcast or by the advisory firm Empower Wealth.

If you have downloaded a free copy of the Make Money Simple again book, then you would have had a MyWealth Portal / MoneySMARTS account set up for you on either of the following two url’s www.tpc.moneysmarts.com.au or ew.moneysmarts.com.au 

If you have every planned to meet or met with a representative of Empower Wealth, then again your email and financial information would have been stored in MyWealth Portal.

Here’s the good news. Because you already have an account set up on the MyWealth Portal desktop version, you can access our new MOORR app with your same login credentials as you already use for the MyWealth Portal. Best of all, your data is going to automatically carry over into the new MOORR app. Cool right!

If it’s been a while and you can’t remember your password, you can go back into the sign up page and tap on the ‘Forgot password’ and it will start the process of re-setting your password to give you access to MOORR so you can check out all the new cool features!.

In the event you are still unsure how your email address is on record with us in the first place, please contact our help desk and we will work with you to get a resolution here. Just know that you can still access the MOORR app now, whilst you wait to hear from us.

provisionSpending.monthlyProvisionSpentContent: This is the actual total spending that took place in each monthly interval from within the planned provisions spending allocated for the year.
provisionSpending.yearlyRemainingProvisionsContent:
This is the previous month’s yearly remaining provisions total plus the current month’s monthly allocated provisions spending, minus the current month’s provisions spent.

This calculation helps you identify just how much of your current cash position is made up of your remaining provisions total on a running monthly basis.
How does this work? Read more about this

regularSpending.accumulatedActualSurplusContent:
This is your current month’s cash position minus the original starting cash position minus the current month’s yearly remaining provision total.

This calculation helps you identify how much surplus money you have captured so far this year, shown on a monthly and rolling target basis.

This could show up as a negative amount if you have spent more than you allocated on regular spending items, so it helps you stay on track with regular spending, by staying in positive territory and builds up over the full 12 month period.
regularSpending.monthlyActualSurplusContent:
This is your current month’s accumulated actual surplus minus the previous month’s accumulated actual surplus.

This calculation helps you identify the amount of surplus that has been captured this month. This could show up as a negative amount if you’ve spent more than you allocated on regular spending items for that month. If you have a negative month, explore what where you overspent and tidy this spending up going forward.
regularSpending.monthlyExcessSurplus/DeficitContent:
This is the current month’s monthly actual surplus minus the current month’s targeted monthly surplus

This calculation helps you identify your monthly excess surplus (or deficit). If it is a deficit for one month here or there, don’t panic, as it could be the result of higher bill payments allocated in that month. It will balance itself out over the full year, so long as you don’t overspend on any expense items in your Money SMARTS yearly plan, or spend money on expense items you haven’t listed at all. This graph will help show if you are on track in not.
regularSpending.primaryAccountRollingBalanceContent:
This is the month-to-month rolling balance of your Primary (offset or High Interest savings) account. It’s the accumulation of the Monthly Surplus balances, either adding (surplus) to or subtracting (deficit) from the previous month’s balance added together with your remaining provisionings total.

This calculation is the Accumulated Actual Surplus that helps you identify and track your progress of accumulating your surplus funds. You want this balance to be growing in line with your targeted surplus each month. Some months might be negative or lower than anticipated if that month has a lot of ‘planned’ bills being paid, so you should know this because you will see those bills being paid from this account or the credit card.

(Just remember if you are spending what you said you would spend and nothing more, then you will be tracking fine)

Let’s get started with your MoneySMARTS Monthly Check-Up! To begin with, enter in the date you want to start tracking your MoneySMARTS balances.

For the next 12 months, you’ll track the opening bank and credit card balance on the selected date for each of your tracked moneySMARTS accounts. Each record will be stored in your Financial Card.

Would you like to perform a Rollover? A rollover commences a new MoneySMARTS tracking period and sets your current period as a past reporting period. This gives you the opportunity to start tracking a fresh 12-month period.

monthlyCheckUp.setUpMoneySMARTSTrackingDescription: To set up your check-up accounts, select ‘Yes’ or ‘No’ in the ‘Track in MoneySMARTS’ field for any bank account, credit card or line of credit you wish to perform monthly check-ups for.
monthlyCheckUp.setUpMoneySMARTSTrackingContent:
MoneySMARTS monthly check-ups allow you to track and understand your money and cashflow position in a shorter timeframe to give you some clearer insights into how well you are progressing and controlling your money. In short, you are assessing the cashflow for the month - money in and money out - and tracking it against your yearly targets. Traditionally, MoneySMARTS check-ups only require you to update your Primary Account bank balance, the balance of your Credit Card account and your total provision spending for the month.

However, modern bank setups mean that people can often run multiple bank accounts, offsets, credit cards and even line of credits. If this is you, as part of your check-up, you may find yourself wanting to track and update the balances of multiple offset accounts.

We’ve now made it possible for you to track multiple account balances within MoneySMARTS instead of a single primary account, by choosing which accounts you wish to update and track on a monthly basis.

asset.optiHelpDetails: Hi, Opti here! I am looking forward to helping you add your {{name}} details. Once set up you will be able to tweak and add more details as you need. Let’s get started with adding your overview information.
asset.optiIncome: Let’s talk about {{name}}’s Income. Here, you can enter any rental income or any adhoc related income. If this is not relevant, you can leave it blank.

asset.optiIncome2Regular: Let’s talk about your card Income. Here, you can enter any regular income or any adhoc related income. If this is not relevant, you can leave it blank.
asset.optiPA: Next is your expenses attached to this asset. It’s ok for an estimate as you can always come back and tweak if you need.

asset.depreciationTooltip:
The annual total depreciation amount will be included in your “Investment Property Deductions” calculation if the Property Type is set as either Investment Property or Business Use at the end of the specified financial year. Please use these fields only if you have a depreciation schedule for this property.

Note that from 1 July 2017, investors in residential investment properties cannot claim a depreciation deduction for any used or second hand assets (Plant & Equipment - Div 40) acquired after 7:29pm on 9 May 2017. New assets separately purchased by investors, or purchased as part of new residential investment properties, are unaffected by this new measure.
